facts: A08 canonical UTS was reported green before A09.
The application SecretVault boundary predates A09 and contains typed refresh-token, board-capability and device-private-key categories.

A09b corrects the AEAD dependency pin to chacha20poly1305 0.10.1 after canonical UTS proved that 0.11.0 resolves through yanked chacha20 0.10.1 and therefore cannot satisfy the offline resolver acceptance gate.
inferences: A Secret Service protected random vault root plus an AEAD-encrypted typed profile vault avoids making the desktop keyring a high-churn application database.
Fail-closed session-only degradation is safer than silently persisting plaintext secrets when the provider is locked or absent.
proposals: A10 credential/sync provisioning should consume SecretVault and may add a narrowly-scoped passphrase activation flow, never a generic secret IPC.
Provider migration/rotation should be explicit and separately tested rather than auto-rebinding ownership.
unresolved: GNOME unlocked/locked, KWallet Secret Service compatibility and minimal no-provider sessions require multi-host evidence.
Same-user malware and full planner database encryption are outside the A09 at-rest guarantee.
